name: Slagline Salvage Parka — Quilted Shell
description: A floor-length parka assembled from reclaimed industrial insulation batting, mismatched ripstop panels, and heat-tape seams. The outer shell is a patchwork of burnt orange, oil-grey, and faded safety yellow — whatever was available. Stuffed dense enough to trap body heat against -30C wind chill, though the fit is rough and the zipper skips every third tooth.
functionality: Extreme cold insulation rated for sub-zero wind chill; oversized cut fits over bulky chrome arms and spinal rigs without modification.
what_it_says: Survival over style — this person is fighting the lake wind with whatever they could pull together.
story_hooks: A hidden inner pocket contains a folded transit map with three locations marked in grease pencil — none of them transit stops.
The insulation batting is stamped with a Ferrochem facility code; someone cut this out of a condemned building's wall.

physical_description.visual_profile: A voluminous, floor-length silhouette suggesting a wanderer or salvage worker. The parka reads as deliberately utilitarian—heavy, constructed from visible pieced-together panels in contrasting industrial colors. Despite its rough assembly, it commands presence through sheer mass and the honest wear of its materials.
physical_description.fit: Oversized and boxy, with room for layering underneath. The torso is generously cut to accommodate bulk insulation; sleeves are slightly long, designed to cover hands when arms are relaxed. No tailoring—pure function.
physical_description.primary_material: Reclaimed industrial insulation batting (likely cellulose or treated fiberglass core), mismatched ripstop nylon panels, heat-tape seams instead of traditional stitching
physical_description.texture: Heavily quilted surface with visible trapezoid or diamond stitch patterns from the batting. Outer panels show the matte, slightly stiff texture of weathered ripstop. Seams are rough and tactile—heat-tape creates a ridge-like texture along stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Chaotic patchwork primary palette: burnt orange, oil-grey, faded safety yellow. No intentional pattern—colors appear random and salvaged. Discoloration and fading suggest exposure to UV and industrial residue.
physical_description.closures: Front zipper with visible tooth skipping (non-functional sections). Friction-fit at wrists and collar (no closures, likely rolled or wrapped). Possibly auxiliary cord ties for securing gaps.
distinctive_features: Visible heat-tape seams running along major stress zones
Patchwork outer shell with abrupt color transitions between panels
Quilted batting visible through worn or translucent ripstop sections
Oversized hood with insulation loft, slightly misshapen
Uneven hem—floor-length but crooked, suggesting field alterations
No visible brand marks or logos—purely utilitarian salvage aesthetic
Functional wear: grease stains, scuff marks, minor tears reinforced with patches
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade salvage. This is ungoverned-zone wear—self-assembled, resource-conscious, no commercial origin.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street scavenger, salvage worker, or unaffiliated wanderer in the GLMZ industrial sectors. Wearing this signals survival over status—you inhabit the spaces between corpo zones and feral territory. The visible DIY construction suggests makeshift resilience.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn and weathered. Seams show stress, patches cover prior damage, zippers are temperamental. This is a parka that has earned its scars through actual use in harsh conditions, not aesthetic distressing.
